title: Snacks
question: How do you pick packaged snack foods?
decision: Read the first ingredient; then ask about chips, crackers or popcorn.
why: Ingredients run in order of amount, so the first one leads. Multigrain is not whole grain.
short_answer: Ingredients run in order of amount, so the first one is the most. A whole grain, vegetable or bean should come first. Multigrain does not mean whole grain. For one snack, ask about chips, crackers or popcorn.
detail: Under 21 CFR 101.4, ingredients are listed in descending order of predominance. FDA draft guidance says the ingredient list should show whether the first ingredient is a whole grain. Multigrain products are often made with several refined grains. Some veggie chips are potato flour colored with vegetable powder or extract, and the ingredients show it. Front-of-package claims and pictures can mislead, so the ingredient list settles it.
kristy_take: The snack aisle reads best one product at a time. Chips, crackers and popcorn each have a card of their own.
cart_pick: A snack with a whole grain listed first
buying_tips: Read the first ingredient before the front of the bag.
Look for a whole grain, vegetable or bean listed first.
Read “multigrain” as several grains, not whole grains.
watch_out: Front-of-package claims and pictures can mislead; the ingredient list settles it.

labels_decoded.meaning: Several grains, often refined ones; it does not mean whole grain.
Powder or extract that colors a chip; check whether potato flour comes first.

tier_note: Vegetable powder colors potato flour, so the chip is mostly potato.
